Variants.Content: Entry The Seven Kingdoms often trade gold dragons, silver deer and bronze stars. In addition to the face value, the weight, fineness, origin and whether the coins can be accepted by local merchants are equally important. Nobles used land and taxes to secure loans, merchants used goods, ships and credit to turn around, and knights might use Debt is not only a matter of money, but also the relationship between marriage alliances, loyalty, hostages and urban politics. Small people will feel the distant decision of kings in food prices and copper coin shortages, and the Iron Bank can turn a loan into pressure across the sea.

Merchants and travelers feel barriers, ransoms, and information prices from currency and debt, while priests and scholars focus on how it shapes legitimacy; the same decision rarely has the same weight in the eyes of different classes.
